cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith. Paul urged him to stay on at Ephesus and look after the church there. Now Paul gets VERY practical: how do you talk to the people in a church family?

cards.question: Say an older man in the church needs correcting. Paul tells Timothy not to rebuke him. So what should Timothy do instead?

answers.text: Appeal to him as to a father
Let the other elders handle it
Wait for him to notice himself

cards.question: Paul keeps the family picture going. Treat younger men as ___ and older women as ___.

cards.text: And younger women as sisters, with absolute purity. Then Paul zooms in on one part of that family: "Honor the widows who are truly widows."

cards.question: A widow has children or grandchildren. Paul says the church should step in and care for her first. True or false?

cards.text: Paul puts family first: her children and grandchildren must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents. Mother Miller baked for her family for YEARS, and I'm just saying, somebody owes that woman a cookie.

cards.question: When children and grandchildren repay a parent or grandparent like this, how does God see it?

cards.text: Now Paul describes the widow who is truly in need. She's left all alone.

cards.question: A widow who is truly in need and left all alone. Where does Paul say she puts her hope?

cards.text: And she continues night and day in her petitions and prayers. Night AND day, friend, and I can't keep my eyes on an oven timer for twelve minutes.

cards.question: Then Paul shows the opposite picture: a widow who lives for pleasure. What does he say about her?

answers.text: She is dead even while alive
She is free to live as she likes
She should be cared for first

cards.text: Paul tells Timothy to give these instructions to the believers, so they will be above reproach. Then he turns to anyone who doesn't provide for his own, especially his own household, and Paul does NOT whisper this one.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who won't provide for his own household has ___ the faith.
Paul also says that person is worse than an unbeliever. True or false?

cards.text: Next, Paul tells Timothy which widows should be enrolled. Not every widow goes on the list.

cards.question: For a widow to be enrolled, how old does Paul say she should be?
She should also be faithful to her husband and well known for good ___.

cards.text: Paul lists them: bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints, bringing relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work. My résumé says "stamped cookies, then sat in a drawer," and I'm reading hers like, MA'AM, you're overqualified.
But the younger widows? Paul tells Timothy to refuse to enroll them, and he explains why.

cards.question: Why does Paul tell Timothy to refuse to enroll the younger widows?

answers.text: Their passions may pull them from Christ
They can still find work to support themselves
The church has no room left on the list

cards.text: Then they'd want to marry, and Paul says that brings judgment, because they're setting aside their first faith. And Paul has one more worry, about how they'd spend their days.

cards.question: Paul says that if the younger widows are enrolled, they'll fill their days with every good work. True or false?

cards.text: Paul says they'd learn to be idle, going from house to house as gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention. Friend, that's not a visit, that's a group chat with legs.

cards.question: So what does Paul advise the younger widows to do instead?

answers.text: Stay single and serve the church

cards.text: Marry, have children and manage their households. Paul says that denies the adversary occasion for slander.

cards.question: Paul says this is just a warning, and none of the younger widows have turned aside yet. True or false?

cards.text: Paul says some have already turned aside to follow Satan. Then he gives one last instruction, for any believing woman who has dependent widows.

cards.question: Paul says a believing woman with dependent widows should hand them over to the church. True or false?
She must assist them and not let the church be burdened. That way the church can help the widows who are truly in ___.

findings.problem: The right answer 'She is dead even while alive' is the passage's vivid paradox in Bible-style wording. The two wrong answers are plain modern phrasing ('free to live as she likes', 'cared for first'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question says 'anyone who won't provide for his own household.' Verse 8 says 'does not provide.' 'Won't' adds refusal, which the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Timothy 5:9-10, but its right answer, 'deeds', comes only from 5:10. 'Faithful to her husband' (5:9) is part of the question, not the answer.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Paul has one more worry, about how they'd spend their days' tells the baker the next point is negative. That rules out True on the following true-or-false card ('they'll fill their days with every good work').

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The statement says 'none of the younger widows have turned aside yet,' so marking it False claims that some younger widows turned aside. Verse 15 says only 'some have already turned aside to follow Satan.' It doesn't say who the 'some' are.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
